chunks.title: kinetic

chunks.text: Let's just consider a person running along a road.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And so here's our runner and here's our road.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And what we want to do is be able to describe the position, the velocity, the acceleration

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: of this runner.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: In order to do that, we need our first mathematical tool, which is a coordinate system.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: What is a coordinate system?

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Well, the first thing that we want to choose is an origin.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: We can pick the origin anywhere we want.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: That's a degree of freedom.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So let's choose a point along our road as our origin.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: The next thing to do is to choose an axis.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Well the road is naturally defining an axis for our problem and so we'll call this the

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: x-axis.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Now along with that axis, we want to divide that up into some type of units so we might

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: divide our axis like this.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And what's important here is to introduce a positive coordinate direction.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And so the way I'll do that is I'll call this the plus x and on this side of the origin,

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: x is negative.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Now the third most important thing is that we're going to talk about vectors in physics.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So we want a choice of unit vector.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Now because it's only one dimensional motion, we only need one unit vector.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So what that means is a choice of unit vector at every point.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Let's just consider a point here, p1.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So our unit vector, I'll call it i hat 1.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Now let's pick another point here.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: We'll call this the point p2 and over here we'll choose a unit vector i hat 2.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So every single point in space has a unit vector.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: Now what's unique about this one dimensional linear Cartesian coordinate system is the

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: following.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: These unit vectors have the same magnitude.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: A unit vector by definition has magnitude 1.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And they're pointing in the same direction.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So if two vectors have the same magnitude and point in the same direction, they're equal.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So what makes this coordinate system unique, this Cartesian coordinate system that at every

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: single point, no matter where we are, the unit vectors point in the positive direction,

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: because they have the same magnitude and direction, all of these unit vectors are equal.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: And we call that i hat.

chunks.title: kinetic
chunks.text: So symbolically, we may draw a picture and indicate our unit vector in the positive

chunks.title: kinetic

chunks.title: kinetic
